docs.title: Documentation
docs.description: How to use Docenti, from first sign-in to exporting your dossier.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.intro: Docenti keeps your data on this computer and works without internet. With an institution account you can also sync between devices and get the official templates.
items: On the sign-in screen, open the "Server" tab and enter your institution's server address. When you save, the app checks the server and returns to the "Sign in" tab.
On the "Sign in" tab, type your email and click "Send code". Then enter the 6-digit code you received by email.
On your first sign-in, enter your name. It appears in the app and in reports.
Without an account, use "Continue as Guest": everything works on this computer, but without sync or official templates.

collections.title: Collections and structure
collections.intro: A collection is a dossier, for example "2026 Progression". It is organized into groups, subgroups and categories.
items: On the home page, click "New collection" to start from scratch or "From template" to start from a ready-made structure.
Inside the collection, use "New group", "New sub-group" and "New category" to build the structure.
Use the edit button (pencil) to rename, set minimum and maximum points, or reorder items.
Deleting a category only unlinks its documents: they stay in your library.

scoring.title: Scoring
scoring.intro: Each category has a rule that defines how much each linked document is worth.
items: Flat: a number of points per document.
Hours: points for every N hours entered on the document.
Capped: a flat or hours rule, with a cap on the category's total.
Capped per document: a flat or hours rule, with a cap for each document.
A document's "Quantity" field multiplies its points — use 2 when a single certificate covers two activities.
Subgroups and groups can have minimum and maximum points. Anything above the maximum isn't counted and shows as "Exceeded"; below the minimum shows "Incomplete".
A group can have a surplus bonus: a percentage of the points earned above the group's minimum.

documents.title: Documents and library
documents.intro: The library holds all your supporting documents. A document can be linked to one or more categories, in any collection.
items: In "Documents", click "New document", fill in the details, then use "Attach" to add the file.
Use "Link" to associate the document with categories. The "Unfiled" tab shows documents without a category yet.
Select several documents to assign tags or link categories all at once.
Files placed directly in your documents folder are detected: the app lets you know and offers to import them.
A document marked "On another device" has its file only on another computer. Use "Locate file…" to point to where it is on this one.

templates.title: Templates
templates.intro: A template is the ready-made structure of a collection: groups, subgroups, categories and scoring rules.
items: Official templates come from your institution's server and are updated automatically.
Imported templates are .json files you received; use "Import template" to add them.
When creating a collection from a template, you can add a ZIP of documents: the app matches the files to the expected documents and links them for you.
To share the structure of one of your collections, use "Export as template" inside it.

exporting.title: Exporting
exporting.intro: On the "Export" screen, pick a collection to see the report preview.
items: The report can be generated as PDF, Excel (.xlsx), CSV or JSON.
"Export documents (Stitched)" creates a ZIP with one PDF per category, merging its documents.
"Export documents (Individual)" creates a ZIP with each document as its own file, in folders by group, subgroup and category.
The JSON file is what someone else uses to check your collection on the "Reviews" screen.

reviews.title: Reviews
reviews.intro: Reviews let you check someone else's collection from the .json file they exported.
items: Click "Import collection (.json)". The copy is read-only and never mixes with your own collections.
The app recalculates the scores. "Scores verified" means the numbers match the file's data — not that the documents are authentic.
Differences between the sent and recalculated values are marked on each item. In that case, confirm with the sender before approving.

sync.title: Sync
sync.intro: With an account, your changes are sent to the server and reach your other devices.
items: The indicator in the sidebar shows whether everything is synced or how many changes are waiting.
Without a connection, keep working as usual: changes are kept and sent when the server is back.
Inside a collection, the "Synced" / "Local only" button controls whether it goes to the server. Local-only collections stay on this computer.

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: "Settings" holds your profile and the app's preferences.
items: Profile: name, email, and the folder where your documents are stored. Changing the folder moves your current files to the new one.
Preferences: theme, language and the server address.
Switching to another institution's server signs you out. Your data stays on this computer and comes back when you return to the previous server.

support.title: Support
support.description: Where to get help when something isn't working.

server.title: Your server
server.runBy: This server is the responsibility of {{institution}}.
server.dependsOn: Sign-in, email codes, sync and official templates depend on the server. Problems with any of these should be raised with the institution.
server.noContact: Contact {{institution}}'s IT department or support team.
server.noServer: No server configured. The app works normally on this computer, but without sign-in, sync or official templates.
server.guest: You're in guest mode, with no connection to your institution's server. To use sign-in, sync and official templates, log out and sign in with your email.

checks.title: Before asking for help
items: Server not responding: keep using the app as usual. Your changes are kept and synced when the connection is back.
Code didn't arrive: check your spam folder, wait a few minutes and request a new code.
"Session expired": click "Sign in again" in the sidebar. Your data isn't affected.
"Different server": check the server address in Settings → Preferences.
File not found: in the library, use "Locate file…" on the document.

institution.title: Your institution
items: You can't sign in or your email isn't accepted

items: The app freezes or closes unexpectedly
Scores calculated incorrectly
Screens or buttons that don't work
Wrong or untranslated text

report.title: Report a problem with the app
report.intro: Problems with the app itself are tracked on GitHub. When you open a report, include:
include: What you were doing, step by step
What you expected to happen and what happened instead
report.privacy: The diagnostic info includes the app version, your system and the server. Your email and session are never included.
